newsitem.title: FINLAND: FISKARS SEES SALES GROWTH, ACQUISITIONS.
newsitem.headline: FISKARS SEES SALES GROWTH, ACQUISITIONS.

text.p: Finnish consumer goods group Fiskars Oy Ab said in a statement on Wednesday it expected ongoing sales growth, and added that its healthy solvency offered good prospects for acquisitions.

"The sales prospects for the corporation's products continue to be good, and the sales growth is expected to continue strong in North America and at a good level in the Nordic countries and the U.K.," Fiskars said in its January-September interim report.
"The good corporate solvency provides excellent opportunities for a further development of operations through internal growth and acquisitions," it said.
In the first nine months of 1996, Fiskars said group profitability had "remained on the previous year's high level."
Profit before extraordinary items and taxes rose 22 percent to 179 million markka, slightly short of the 185 million markka median of analysts' forecasts.
Due to proceeds from the sale of its UPS business, group profit after extraordinary items soared to 581 million markka from 125 million, Fiskars said.
Net sales fell to 1.58 billion markka in January-September from 1.71 billion in the year-ago period, but Fiskars noted that net sales from ongoing operations increased 23 percent.
Fiskars said its two recent acquisitions, Portable Products Inc. in March and Newpoint Corporation in June, had both "perfectly adapted to Fiskars' operating principles."
